preamble: Lowering of the open-mid front vowel /ɛ/ to open /a/. The best-documented case is the late Middle English lowering of short /ɛ/ before /r/ (sterre > star, sterven > starve, kerven > carve, ferre > far). It survives unevenly, sometimes as doublets such as person/parson and vermin/varmint, and as British pronunciations like clerk /klɑːk/ and Derby /ˈdɑːbi/.

examples.note: Late Middle English and Early Modern English lowering of /ɛr/ to /ar/, later /ɑː(r)/.
Dialect doublet showing the same lowering of /ɛr/ to /ar/.
